prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address what happens when StreamableHTTP client reconnection to the SSE stream is unrecoverable: PR #2395 changes the `attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS` bail-out branch in `_handle_reconnection` to construct a JSONRPCError and push it onto `read_stream_writer` so the specific pending request gets a response instead of hanging forever (the branch was previously `pragma: no cover` dead code that just logged and returned). prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the same create_memory_object_stream call for write_stream in src/mcp/server/stdio.py, targeting the same root issue: an unbuffered (buffer size 0) write channel forces the stdout writer to rendezvous with the reader on every message, so a handler cannot queue its final response while an earlier notification (e.g. progress) is still being flushed. #2215 addresses this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as opt-in constructor parameters (default 0, i.e. no behavior change unless a caller explicitly passes a nonzero value). #2654 addresses it by hardcoding the write-stream buffer to 1, fixing the blocking behavior by default for every caller, and ships a BlockingStdout test harness that reproduces the progress-notification deadlock and asserts it no longer occurs. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2654 fixes the blocking-write bug for all callers by default (buffer size hardcoded to 1), whereas #2215 only adds an opt-in parameter that defaults to the original value of 0, so no existing caller actually gets the fix without further code changes. #2654 also adds a concrete regression test (BlockingStdout simulating a slow stdout during a progress notification) proving the specific deadlock scenario is resolved, while #2215's test changes are incidental to the signature change. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug: WWW-Authenticate header parsing in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py used naive/substring matching for auth-params instead of properly tokenizing comma-separated, quote-aware auth-params, causing false-positive matches on parameter values. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the entire header (including the scheme token) on top-level commas and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly selects the Bearer scheme's segment before collecting its params, so it correctly handles headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=y'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat param list, without isolating a specific scheme, which would misparse multi-challenge headers containing more than one scheme. members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs modify the same create_memory_object_stream call for write_stream in src/mcp/server/stdio.py, targeting the same root issue: an unbuffered (buffer size 0) write channel forces the stdout writer to rendezvous with the reader on every message, so a handler cannot queue its final response while an earlier notification (e.g. progress) is still being flushed. #2215 addresses this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as opt-in constructor parameters (default 0, i.e. no behavior change unless a caller explicitly passes a nonzero value). #2654 addresses it by hardcoding the write-stream buffer to 1, fixing the blocking behavior by default for every caller, and ships a BlockingStdout test harness that reproduces the progress-notification deadlock and asserts it no longer occurs.

members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address what happens when StreamableHTTP client reconnection to the SSE stream is unrecoverable: PR #2395 changes the `attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS` bail-out branch in `_handle_reconnection` to construct a JSONRPCError and push it onto `read_stream_writer` so the specific pending request gets a response instead of hanging forever (the branch was previously `pragma: no cover` dead code that just logged and returned). clusters.pick_reason: #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the entire header (including the scheme token) on top-level commas and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly selects the Bearer scheme's segment before collecting its params, so it correctly handles headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=y'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat param list, without isolating a specific scheme, which would misparse multi-challenge headers containing more than one scheme. Both use equivalent quote/escape-aware comma-splitting logic, but #3041's segment-then-scheme-select approach covers a case #3012's does not.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs modify the same create_memory_object_stream call for write_stream in src/mcp/server/stdio.py, targeting the same root issue: an unbuffered (buffer size 0) write channel forces the stdout writer to rendezvous with the reader on every message, so a handler cannot queue its final response while an earlier notification (e.g. progress) is still being flushed. #2215 addresses this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as opt-in constructor parameters (default 0, i.e. no behavior change unless a caller explicitly passes a nonzero value). #2654 addresses it by hardcoding the write-stream buffer to 1, fixing the blocking behavior by default for every caller, and ships a BlockingStdout test harness that reproduces the progress-notification deadlock and asserts it no longer occurs.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2395: Both address what happens when StreamableHTTP client reconnection to the SSE stream is unrecoverable: PR #2395 changes the `attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS` bail-out branch in `_handle_reconnection` to construct a JSONRPCError and push it onto `read_stream_writer` so the specific pending request gets a response instead of hanging forever (the branch was previously `pragma: no cover` dead code that just logged and returned). PR #3098 adds a `_unwrap_exception` helper to dig a `StreamableHTTPError` out of an anyio ExceptionGroup and raise it when reconnection fails. Both are fixes for the same root gap — a failed reconnection previously left callers with no usable error — just implemented at different layers (per-request JSON-RPC error vs. raised exception propagated up the task group).

clusters.pick_reason: 2962 adds a has_tool_results guard that skips the id-matching check entirely, so no exception is raised when tool_use has no following tool_result — this matches the SEP-1577 spec cited in its regression test (tool_result must be preceded by tool_use, but tool_use is not required to be followed by tool_result). 3053 touches the same branch but does the opposite: it adds a new explicit raise ValueError(...) for the exact same no-tool_results case, only changing the error message, so it does not fix the reported regression and directly conflicts with 2962's behavior — merging both is impossible since one raises and the other doesn't for the same input.

clusters.pick_reason: #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the entire header (including the scheme token) on top-level commas and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly selects the Bearer scheme's segment before collecting its params, so it correctly handles headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=y'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat param list, without isolating a specific scheme, which would misparse multi-challenge headers containing more than one scheme. Both use equivalent quote/escape-aware comma-splitting logic, but #3041's segment-then-scheme-select approach covers a case #3012's does not.

members.title: Scope HTTP client redirect following to the request's origin
members.author: maxisbey
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying issue: the MCP Python SDK's httpx client currently follows redirects unconditionally (follow_redirects=True), which is a security risk since a malicious/compromised server could redirect requests (including auth headers) to an arbitrary off-origin host. Both PRs change the client to only follow redirects within the same origin as the original MCP endpoint, and both update the same line in docs/client/transports.md describing this behavior. (2 PRs)
